title: Add optional workload annotations/labels for offline bundle build correlation
author: Devon Price
description: Context: For Redwood Private air-gapped installs we now ship signed offline bundles. Support needs a deterministic way to correlate a running cluster (workloads) to the exact offline bundle build that installed it, without requiring customers to upload the full bundle or logs. This PR adds optional annotations/labels to charts so the installer (or operators) can inject a bundle build identifier into Kubernetes objects. Summary: (1) Add a shared helper that renders bundle metadata into standard annotations/labels, (2) plumb through values in each chart with no-op defaults, and (3) document the values and ensure templates don’t change existing output unless the values are set. Details: - New values under global.offlineBundle (all optional): buildId (string), releaseId (string), manifestDigest (string), signerKeyId (string). - New standard keys used across workloads: annotations: redwood.ai/offline-bundle-build-id, redwood.ai/offline-bundle-release-id, redwood.ai/offline-bundle-manifest-digest, redwood.ai/offline-bundle-signer-key-id; labels: redwood.ai/offline-bundle-build-id (kept minimal to avoid label bloat and label length constraints). - All keys are only emitted when the corresponding value is non-empty. - Values are added to: Deployment/StatefulSet pod template metadata + top-level object metadata for easier kubectl queries, and to Jobs/CronJobs where present. - Added a small NOTES.txt section to hint how to query: kubectl get pods -A -l redwood.ai/offline-bundle-build-id=<id>. Motivation: This is the glue needed for support bundles and for triaging verification/upgrade issues (e.g., confirming a cluster is on a specific signed bundle build when the customer can’t export full logs). This aligns with the broader signed offline bundle effort and downstream work in the installer to record/emit build IDs. Testing: helm lint, template snapshot tests for each chart verifying no diff when values unset; new golden tests verifying keys appear when set; validated against a kind cluster by installing with global.offlineBundle.buildId=rbwpriv_2025-11-18. Follow-ups: The installer PR will set these values automatically from the signed manifest/build metadata; docs PR to include recommended query patterns for air-gapped support cases.

review_conversation: Ethan Park: Can we keep label usage minimal? We’ve hit label length/selector constraints in a few customer clusters. Also please ensure we don’t change rendered manifests when values are empty.
Devon Price (author): Yep—labels will only include build-id (short, installer-controlled). All other fields are annotations only. Added snapshot tests verifying no manifest diffs when unset.
Connor O'Brien: Naming: prefer redwood.ai/offline-bundle-build-id vs bundle-build-id for clarity. Also can we add signer key id for post-rotation troubleshooting?
Devon Price (author): Updated keys to redwood.ai/offline-bundle-*, added signerKeyId as annotation only, and documented it in values.yaml + NOTES.
Logan Wright: If we’re going to rely on this in support bundles, we should put it both on pod template metadata and top-level metadata so we can query workloads and pods. Is that covered?
Devon Price (author): Added to both object metadata and pod template metadata for Deployment/StatefulSet/Job/CronJob templates.
Kira Thompson: Please add a short NOTES snippet with the kubectl query so support and customers have a ready command.
Devon Price (author): Added NOTES section with kubectl examples and note that keys appear only when values are set.
Ethan Park: Looks good now. Approved.
Connor O'Brien: Approved; please link this PR in the installer rollout checklist.
Devon Price (author): Linked to ENG-4828 and added note in release train thread.
release_notes: Helm charts: optional annotations/labels can be set to record the offline bundle build ID on Kubernetes workloads for support correlation (no-op unless configured).
